title: JUnit reports from node --test are read: pass, fail and skip per test, nested suites, entities; a file that is not JUnit is refused
Ledger rows are validated on load and a key in two files is refused
--gate-phase N fails while any row of phase N or earlier is not covered, fixed or a reviewed wont
A row whose profile entry disappears is marked orphaned, never deleted, and the parity check fails until reviewed
Every row in the profiles' limitation and capability sections is in the ledger; the seeded files match a fresh seed
Status is computed from the lanes' reports: covered needs a passing positive and negative test on every platform the row names; a skip counts as not run
Any failing test tagged with a row's key makes the row regressed and fails the check
A test tagged with a key no row has fails the check
One grader for every arm: claims block only, vocabulary normalised, refuted and out-of-set claims penalised, labels graded, duplicates counted once

The harness runs cells one at a time in fresh workspaces and records transcript, model, digests, tool versions, turns, tool calls, token split, time and timeouts; the fake arm exercises it with no model
Oracle facts come from LLVM's tools, not reax; the committed tasks match a fresh LLVM run
30 benchmark tasks over the fixture corpus, subjects pinned by digest, with refuted facts to avoid and an adversarial task
Every committed fixture has the size and SHA-256 its manifest records; a changed, missing or unlisted file is reported
Rebuilding the corpus with the pinned zig at the fixed build root gives byte-identical files; a different zig version is refused
Every fixture's header matches its target (container format, machine, word size); the fat and PE helpers refuse other input
reax's read-only operations run inside Assay as core probes (reax.*): the engine guards the path, keys the run by its inputs, stores the result as target-derived evidence the agent can cite
Every local model server is closed cleanly after use (SIGTERM, a grace period, then SIGKILL; exit and freed port confirmed), also when the harness is interrupted; the doctor reports any left behind
Setup fits the local model's context to the memory cap by measuring the server's peak resident memory with the context filled, not by estimating
The hybrid (local worker, Opus plan and review, Codex review, one revision) records every role and grades both the first and the final answer

Live backends (local llama.cpp, Codex CLI, Claude Code CLI) each run standalone and record model, effort, tokens, cost, memory and grade; sign-in, memory-cap and timeout stops are errors, not wrong answers

The local model's answer is never lost to the harness: the output contract and every operation's summary in its system prompt, a search tool like the CLIs' Grep, one nudge when a turn runs out of tokens while reasoning, no-answer as an error, and a diagnostic beside the strict score for claims under the wrong fence
The CLIs start the same way on Linux, macOS and Windows: npm .cmd shims without cmd.exe, prompts over stdin, PATH joined with the OS's delimiter, the whole process tree ended at the deadline

Setup picks llama.cpp's own build for the machine's hardware (Metal, CUDA by driver version, ROCm, Vulkan, Adreno OpenCL, SYCL by choice, CPU always last), falls back when a build does not run on it, and checks every download against its publisher's sha256

On the native libraries LearnHarness ships (ELF glibc and musl, x86_64 and aarch64; Mach-O; PE with delay-load imports; wasm), reax's inventory and core's readers agree with LLVM 18 on architecture, own name, links and the whole export table, and claims about them verify or are refuted

The extra fixtures (a gcc binary with build ID and property notes; a stripped Go program with a module dependency, for Linux and Windows) are committed and pinned by digest; a changed, unlisted or missing file is refused
One operation registry generates docs/operations.md, the tool catalog and the ledger mapping; every documented example runs as a test; a mapping to an unknown or doubly covered row is refused

Every operation's result renders as text, json, jsonl, yaml, markdown or toon; TOON and YAML round-trip through independent decoders (the TOON reference decoder, yaml in 1.2 and 1.1 modes, PyYAML); --filter-output keeps named paths and --llms lists every operation with an example that runs
List results page statelessly with offset and limit: pages of any size reassemble the whole list, page.next is the next offset or null, and out-of-range paging arguments are refused
The core verifier checks native.arch and native.exports claims with core's own readers, verified against LLVM's reading of every fixture; an export is refuted only when the list is complete

Every connection authenticates with the token from the daemon's token file, compared in constant time; a missing, wrong, previous-instance or late token is refused, and the token appears in no log, reply or argument
At the connection cap a new connection gets a retryable daemon_busy frame, and reax's client reports daemon_busy, not daemon_unauthorized
reax serve answers ping and status over a Unix socket (a named pipe on Windows), and shutdown removes its lock, endpoint, socket and token; a stopped daemon is reported not running
With --tcp the daemon binds only 127.0.0.1 or ::1 and is unreachable on other addresses; any other host is refused before a file or socket is created
One daemon per REAX_HOME: a second start and racing starts leave exactly one daemon, the rest refused with daemon_running
A lock whose pid is dead or whose endpoint is unreachable, or one left by a killed daemon, is recovered and reported; a live daemon's lock is never broken
The token file is 0600 and its directory 0700, owned by the user; a group- or world-writable home or token file is refused
The engine contract and registry: discovery with version and binary digest, timeout, cancellation and structured errors, against fake engines
The LLVM provider runs llvm-nm inside the sandbox; its parsed defined symbols (name, type letter, address) equal the committed key; where no sandbox is enforced it fails closed
session.index stores inventory.symbols for a target keyed by its digest; search.symbols returns exactly the stored symbols, and an FTS5 query exactly those whose names contain the text
pm.db is created and migrated in one transaction; a failed migration leaves the previous version; a newer on-disk version is refused unmodified; the data survives a restart in another process
A child runs under an enforced policy: an allowed read succeeds; a write outside the scratch directory and a loopback connection are refused, seen from outside the child
Where no sandbox is enforced, work that requires one is refused with sandbox_unavailable and nothing runs; work that does not require one runs labelled unenforced

Cancelling a queued job means it never starts; cancelling a running job stops it: a sandboxed engine's process tree is killed and an open pm.db write is rolled back; a job that finished first stays succeeded; a client disconnect cancels only that client's jobs; shutdown cancels and drains all

job.submit, status, list, wait, result and cancel work only after an authenticated hello; unknown or evicted ids give job_not_found; results stay within the result budget; operations not in the registry cannot be run by reax serve

Jobs run through the daemon under a bounded queue: daemon-wide and per-connection caps refuse with the retryable job_queue_full; running caps per class keep a slot for cheap work; start order follows the documented round-robin rule, checked against a separately written reference model, and while a connection has a job that could start, no other connection starts two jobs before it starts one
A job past its deadline (counted from its start) ends timed_out with job_timeout, distinct from job_cancelled, and its engine tree is killed; a job that finishes in time is unaffected

Write jobs run one at a time; a pm.db write lock held by another process gives the retryable pm_busy without blocking the daemon's other connections, and a job waiting for the lock can be cancelled with nothing stored
